topicName: Ansible Vault: Encrypting Files, Strings, and Passwords
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Ansible Vault: Encrypting Files, Strings, and Passwords"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When managing infrastructure as code with Ansible, sensitive data such as API tokens, database passwords, and SSH keys must be handled securely. Ansible Vault is a built-in feature that allows you to encrypt entire files, specific variables, or individual strings within your playbooks."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Encrypting Entire Files"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The most common use case for Ansible Vault is encrypting YAML files containing variables. You can encrypt an existing file using the ansible-vault encrypt command."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"ansible-vault encrypt secrets.yml"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You will be prompted to provide a secure password. Once completed, the contents of 'secrets.yml' will be completely unreadable if viewed normally. To view the contents without permanently decrypting the file, use the view command:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"ansible-vault view secrets.yml"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Encrypting Individual Strings"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes you only want to protect a single variable inside an unencrypted file, such as a database password. You can encrypt a single string using the encrypt_string subcommand."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ansible-vault encrypt_string --vault-id default --name 'db_password' 'SuperSecretPassword123'"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"This generates a YAML-compatible encrypted block that you can copy and paste directly into your playbook or variable file:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"db_password: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          3338303362366665...
          ..."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Running Playbooks with Encrypted Data"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"When executing a playbook that references encrypted files or variables, Ansible will require the vault password to decrypt them at runtime. You can prompt the user for the password interactively using the --ask-vault-pass flag:"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"ansible-playbook site.yml --ask-vault-pass"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Automated Execution Using Password Files"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"For automated CI/CD pipelines, interactive prompts will cause the playbook execution to hang. Instead, you can store the vault password in a local text file and reference it via the command line."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"ansible-playbook site.yml --vault-password-file .vault_pass.txt"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always add your vault password files to your .gitignore to prevent accidental exposure in version control."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can configure 'vault_password_file' inside your ansible.cfg file to avoid passing it via the command line every time."}]
